scope: Two N32 wings, two motion-arm variants, eight local coupled poles and two independently computed local speed brackets. Virtual influence geometry and all physical parameters remain fixed.

plan.scope: Source-convention sensitivity only. Physical force-point kinematics is explicit in unsteady equations 29–31; physical control-point motion is tested separately. Wind-aligned influence geometry and all physical parameters remain fixed. Do not infer experimental agreement.
plan.decision: Interpret primary-source equations and physical trajectory tests; do not pick a variant based on closeness to the published flutter speed.
retained_model_assumptions: Discrete Glauert geometry and wind-aligned vortex/control field locations unchanged.
Only kinematic arms vary; physical force/moment arms already unchanged and physical.
All source properties, real/apparent inertia, gravity, stall and empirical lag retained.
Local branch tracking only; no complete spectrum.

material_trajectory.scope: Checks material-point kinematics and the algebraic distinction from virtual wind-aligned arms. It does not identify the convention in the unavailable original ASWING implementation.

source_review.distinction: Steady equations 64/67 and 155–157 use wind-aligned influence locations; unsteady 29–31 give physical quarter-chord material motion. Combining those approximations is not completely specified by these excerpts.
source_review.derivation: For pure spanwise pitch, virtual-minus-physical sampled velocity is ell*omega*(sin(alpha)*c_hat+(1-cos(alpha))*n_hat). The normal difference is second order at zero incidence; the first-order chordwise term multiplies base circulation in Kutta–Joukowski lift.

decision: Changing only motion arms moves this local crossing by less than 0.02 m/s and farther from the published value. These variants cannot account for the approximately 2 m/s discrepancy under the retained influence geometry. No production convention is selected or calibrated from these results.
limitations: This changes only elastic motion arms. The cases have zero rigid rates; a production change must preserve rigid/elastic motion equivalence.

Virtual vortex/control influence geometry is held fixed; induced, gust, volume and engine sampling locations are not relocated. The variants are scoped mixed approximations, not identified original-ASWING implementations.
Local branch searches do not classify the complete spectrum or establish a finer aerodynamic mesh limit.
Source property/operating-setting conflicts and exact original ASWING input remain unresolved; no experimental agreement is claimed.
